Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ১) Which neuroglial cell lines the cavities of CNS?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
Ependymal cells are specialized neuroglial cells that line the ventricles of the brain and central canal of the spinal cord. They are typically ciliated simple cuboidal to columnar cells and help circulate and regulate cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

  • Oligodendrocytes → form myelin in the CNS.

  • Astrocytes → structural/metabolic support and contribute to the blood–brain barrier.

  • Ependymal cells → line CNS cavities.

  • Microglia → resident macrophages of the CNS.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Ependymal cell → lines ventricles + central canal

  • Oligodendrocyte → CNS myelin

  • Astrocyte → BBB/support

  • Microglia → phagocytosis

Exam Pearl:
Cavities of CNS are lined by ependymal cells.

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ২) What type of neurons are present in olfactory mucosa?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
The olfactory receptor cells in the olfactory mucosa are bipolar neurons. Their dendrites extend toward the epithelial surface and end in olfactory cilia, while their axons pass through the cribriform plate to synapse in the olfactory bulb.

  • Bipolar neurons → olfactory receptor cells and retinal bipolar cells.

  • Pseudounipolar → sensory neurons of dorsal root ganglia.

  • Multipolar → most motor neurons and many CNS neurons.

  • Unipolar → uncommon in humans.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Olfactory receptor neuron → Bipolar

  • Retina → Bipolar cells

  • Dorsal root ganglion → Pseudounipolar

  • Anterior horn motor neuron → Multipolar

Exam Pearl:
Olfactory mucosa contains bipolar receptor neurons.

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ৩) Which is the thickest layer of epidermis?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
The stratum spinosum is generally regarded as the thickest cellular layer of the epidermis. It is composed of several layers of keratinocytes connected by prominent desmosomes, which give the cells a “spiny” appearance in histological sections. OpenStax specifically identifies the stratum spinosum as the thickest layer in the illustrated epidermis.

  • Epidermal layers, deep → superficial:
    Stratum basale → Stratum spinosum → Stratum granulosum → Stratum lucidum → Stratum corneum

    Stratum basale → deepest layer; usually a single row of mitotically active cells.
    Stratum spinosum → multiple layers of keratinocytes; generally the thickest cellular layer.
    Stratum granulosum → contains keratohyalin granules.
    Stratum lucidum → present only in thick skin, such as palms and soles.
    Stratum corneum → most superficial layer; consists of dead, keratinized corneocytes and may become very thick in thick skin. OpenStax notes that it commonly contains about 15–30 cell layers.

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ৪) Which of the following sense organ of skin is responsible for sense of touch?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
Meissner's corpuscles are specialized mechanoreceptors responsible for fine/discriminative touch, particularly in glabrous skin such as the fingertips, palms, and soles. They are located within the dermal papillae.

  • Merkel's discs → light touch, pressure, and texture discrimination.

  • Pacinian corpuscles → deep pressure and vibration.

  • Ruffini endings → skin stretch and sustained pressure.

  • Meissner's corpuscles → fine touch and low-frequency vibration.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Receptor Main sensation
Meissner corpuscle Fine touch
Merkel disc Light touch/pressure, texture
Pacinian corpuscle Deep pressure + vibration
Ruffini ending Skin stretch

Exam Pearl:
Sense of fine touch → Meissner's corpuscles.

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ৫) How many types of cells are present in parathyroid gland?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
The parathyroid gland contains two main types of parenchymal cells:

  1. Chief (principal) cells → produce parathyroid hormone (PTH) and are the predominant cells.

  2. Oxyphil cells → larger, eosinophilic cells with abundant mitochondria; their exact function is less well established.

So, the standard histological answer is 2 types of cells.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Chief cells → PTH secretion

  • Oxyphil cells → eosinophilic, mitochondria-rich

  • Parathyroid → 2 main cell types

Exam Pearl:
Parathyroid gland = 2 main cell types: chief + oxyphil.

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ৬) What is the principal product of zona glomerulosa?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
The zona glomerulosa is the outermost layer of the adrenal cortex and primarily produces mineralocorticoids, especially aldosterone.

The adrenal cortex follows the mnemonic:

GFR → Salt, Sugar, Sex

  • Zona Glomerulosa → Aldosterone → Salt

  • Zona Fasciculata → Cortisol → Sugar

  • Zona Reticularis → Androgens (DHEA) → Sex

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Glomerulosa → Aldosterone

  • Fasciculata → Cortisol

  • Reticularis → DHEA/androgens

  • Adrenal medulla → Catecholamines

Exam Pearl:
Zona glomerulosa = aldosterone.

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ৭) Which is a protein or peptide hormone?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
Oxytocin is a peptide hormone synthesized in the hypothalamus and released from the posterior pituitary. It promotes uterine contraction during labor and milk ejection during breastfeeding.

The other options are not peptide hormones:

  • Cortisol → steroid hormone

  • Thyroxine (T4) → amino-acid-derived thyroid hormone

  • Dopamine → catecholamine/neurotransmitter

  • Oxytocin → nonapeptide hormone

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Peptide: Oxytocin, ADH, insulin, PTH

  • Steroid: Cortisol, aldosterone, testosterone

  • Amino-acid derived: T3/T4, catecholamines

Exam Pearl:
Oxytocin = peptide hormone (nonapeptide).

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ৮) What is the source of ANP?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
Atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) is produced mainly by the atrial cardiomyocytes of the heart in response to atrial stretch, particularly when blood volume or venous return increases.

ANP promotes:

  • Natriuresis → ↑ Na⁺ excretion

  • Diuresis → ↑ water excretion

  • Vasodilation

  • ↓ Renin, aldosterone, and ADH activity

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • ANP → atrial myocardium

  • BNP → mainly ventricular myocardium

  • ANP → ↓ blood volume and blood pressure

Exam Pearl:
ANP = Atrial Natriuretic Peptide → source is the heart (atria).

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ৯) Cortisol has permissive action on which hormone?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
Cortisol has a permissive effect on glucagon and other hormones involved in maintaining blood glucose. It enhances the metabolic actions of glucagon and catecholamines, helping maintain adequate blood glucose during fasting and stress.

A permissive effect means cortisol itself may not produce the full response but allows or enhances the action of another hormone.

  • Glucagon → cortisol enhances its glucose-raising effects.

  • GH → cortisol does not have the classic permissive relationship tested here.

  • TSH/ACTH → no classic permissive action in this context.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Cortisol → permissive to glucagon + catecholamines

  • Cortisol → supports gluconeogenesis

  • Cortisol → increases vascular responsiveness to catecholamines

Exam Pearl:
Cortisol has a permissive action on glucagon and catecholamines.

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ১০) Features of UMNL excludes....?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
Upper motor neuron lesion (UMNL) typically causes spasticity, hyperreflexia, positive Babinski sign, and clonus.

Muscle wasting is not a typical feature of UMNL. Significant muscle wasting is more characteristic of a lower motor neuron lesion (LMNL) due to denervation, although mild disuse atrophy can occur in chronic UMNL.

  • Spasticity → UMNL

  • Positive Babinski sign → UMNL

  • Clonus → UMNL

  • Marked muscle wasting → LMNL

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

UMNL LMNL
Spasticity Flaccidity
Hyperreflexia Hyporeflexia
Babinski positive Babinski absent
Clonus No clonus
Minimal disuse atrophy Marked muscle wasting
No fasciculations Fasciculations

Exam Pearl:
UMNL = spastic, hyperreflexic, Babinski positive; marked muscle wasting → LMNL.

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ১১) Which nuclei of hypothalamus serves as satiety centre?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
The ventromedial nucleus (VMN) of the hypothalamus is classically regarded as the satiety centre. Activation of this centre suppresses food intake and promotes satiety.

  • Ventromedial nucleus → Satiety centre

  • Lateral hypothalamic area → Hunger/feeding centre

  • Paraventricular nucleus → autonomic/endocrine regulation

  • Supraoptic nucleus → mainly ADH synthesis

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Hypothalamic area Main function
Ventromedial nucleus Satiety
Lateral hypothalamic area Hunger/feeding
Supraoptic nucleus ADH
Paraventricular nucleus Oxytocin + autonomic/endocrine functions

Exam Pearl:
Ventromedial nucleus = satiety centre; lateral hypothalamus = hunger centre.

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ১২) What is the location of lesion in Parkinson's disease?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
Parkinson’s disease is caused primarily by degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta, which is functionally part of the basal ganglia circuitry. This leads to reduced dopamine in the striatum, producing the characteristic bradykinesia, rigidity, resting tremor, and postural instability.

  • Basal ganglia → involved in Parkinson’s disease.

  • Reticular formation → arousal, autonomic and motor functions.

  • Limbic system → emotion and memory.

  • Internal capsule → major white-matter pathway; lesions cause characteristic motor/sensory deficits.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Parkinson’s → substantia nigra pars compacta degeneration

  • ↓ Dopamine → striatum

  • Lewy bodies → α-synuclein

  • Classic signs → resting tremor + rigidity + bradykinesia

Exam Pearl:
Parkinson’s disease = degeneration of substantia nigra → basal ganglia dysfunction.

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ১৩) Which is used to investigate cutaneous Type-1 hypersensitivity?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
The skin prick test is used to investigate Type I (immediate, IgE-mediated) hypersensitivity, especially IgE-mediated allergy to substances such as foods, pollens, dust mites, and animal dander.

  • Prick test → Type I hypersensitivity → IgE-mediated

  • Patch test → Type IV hypersensitivity → allergic contact dermatitis

  • Dermatoscopy → examination of pigmented/skin lesions

  • Diascopy → assesses whether erythema blanches with pressure

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Test Main use
Prick test Type I / IgE
Patch test Type IV / delayed
Diascopy Blanching of skin lesions
Dermatoscopy Detailed examination of skin lesions

Exam Pearl:
Type I hypersensitivity → Skin prick test.

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ১৪) Which is not true about features of malignant melanoma?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
The classic warning signs of malignant melanoma are summarized by the ABCDE criteria:

  • A — Asymmetry

  • B — Border irregularity

  • C — Colour variation/irregular colour

  • D — Diameter >6 mm (classically)

  • E — Evolution/elevation or change over time

Therefore, a regular border is not a typical feature of malignant melanoma.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Melanoma → asymmetry

  • Irregular border

  • Variegated colour

  • Increasing diameter

  • Evolution in size, shape, or colour

Exam Pearl:
Melanoma = ABCDE; a regular border is NOT characteristic.

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ১৫) Which is non invasive melanoma?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
Melanoma in situ is a non-invasive melanoma because the malignant melanocytes are confined to the epidermis and have not invaded through the basement membrane into the dermis.

The other options are invasive melanoma subtypes:

  • Nodular melanoma → rapidly growing, invasive.

  • Subungual melanoma → usually an acral melanoma involving the nail unit and can be invasive.

  • Acral lentiginous melanoma → occurs on palms, soles, and nail apparatus; can become invasive.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Melanoma in situ → confined to epidermis → non-invasive

  • Invasive melanoma → crosses basement membrane

  • Melanoma in situ → excellent prognosis when completely excised

Exam Pearl:
Non-invasive melanoma = Melanoma in situ.

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ১৬) Which form of topical corticosteroids are preferred for chronic eczema?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
For chronic eczema, topical corticosteroid ointments are generally preferred because they are more occlusive and emollient, improving hydration and penetration of the steroid through the thickened, dry skin typical of chronic eczema.

  • Ointment → best for chronic, dry, lichenified eczema

  • Cream → useful for acute/subacute or moist lesions

  • Lotion → useful for hairy or large areas

  • Drops → not a standard preparation for eczema

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Chronic + dry eczema → ointment

  • Acute/weeping eczema → cream/lotion may be preferred

  • Ointments → greater occlusion and penetration

Exam Pearl:
Chronic dry eczema → topical corticosteroid ointment.

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ১৭) Which is functional stroke mimics?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
A functional stroke mimic refers to Functional Neurological Disorder (FND), where stroke-like neurological deficits occur without an acute structural brain lesion. Typical examples include functional weakness, sensory loss, or speech disturbance.

Among the given options:

  • Subdural hematoma → structural lesion

  • Demyelination → organic neurological disease; can mimic stroke but is not functional

  • Cerebral abscess → structural/infective lesion

  • Encephalitis → inflammatory/infective brain disease

Therefore, none of the listed options is a functional stroke mimic.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Functional stroke mimic → Functional neurological disorder

  • Other common stroke mimics → hypoglycemia, seizure/postictal paralysis, migraine, brain tumor

  • Demyelinating disease → organic stroke mimic

Exam Pearl:
If the question specifically asks “functional stroke mimic,” the expected answer is Functional Neurological Disorder (FND). This MCQ appears to have an incorrect/missing option.

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ১৮) Which is 1st line drug in absence seizure?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
Ethosuximide is the first-line drug for absence seizures, particularly typical absence seizures without other seizure types. It works mainly by reducing T-type calcium currents in thalamic neurons, suppressing the abnormal thalamocortical oscillations responsible for absence seizures.

  • Ethosuximide → first-line for typical absence seizures

  • Sodium valproate → preferred when absence seizures coexist with generalized tonic-clonic or myoclonic seizures

  • Lamotrigine → alternative option

  • Levetiracetam → not the classic first-line choice for typical absence seizures

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Absence → Ethosuximide

  • Absence + GTCS/myoclonic → Valproate

  • Mechanism → T-type Ca²⁺ channel blockade

Exam Pearl:
Typical absence seizure → Ethosuximide.

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ১৯) Which is common organism for meningitis in pre school child?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
For a preschool-aged child, the classically tested organism causing bacterial meningitis is Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib), particularly in unvaccinated children.

  • H. influenzae type b → classically associated with meningitis in young children/preschool age

  • Group B Streptococcus → mainly neonates

  • E. coli → mainly neonatal meningitis

  • Proteus → not a common cause of community-acquired meningitis in children

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Age group Common bacterial meningitis organisms
Neonate GBS, E. coli, Listeria
Infant/young child S. pneumoniae, Hib, N. meningitidis
Adolescent N. meningitidis, S. pneumoniae

Exam Pearl:
Preschool child + classic exam question → H. influenzae type b.

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ২০) Which is the most common cause of dizziness in those under 65 years?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
In people younger than 65 years, anxiety and other psychological causes are among the commonest causes of dizziness. Anxiety can produce a sensation of light-headedness, imbalance, or non-specific dizziness, particularly when no clear vestibular or cardiovascular cause is found.

  • Anxiety → common cause of non-specific dizziness in younger adults.

  • Hypoglycemia → can cause dizziness, but is not the most common overall cause.

  • Hypocalcemia → may cause neurological/muscular symptoms but is uncommon as a cause of dizziness.

  • Visual disturbance → can contribute to imbalance but is not the commonest cause.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • <65 years → anxiety/psychological causes are common

  • Older adults → consider multifactorial causes, medications, cardiovascular and neurological disease.

  • Always distinguish vertigo from light-headedness and imbalance.

Exam Pearl:
Dizziness in a younger adult → anxiety is a common cause.

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ২১) Diffuse soft goitre with bruit indicates.....?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
A diffuse, soft goitre with a thyroid bruit is a classic feature of Graves' disease. The bruit results from increased thyroid vascularity and blood flow caused by TSH-receptor stimulation by autoantibodies.

  • Graves' disease → diffuse soft goitre + bruit + thyrotoxicosis

  • Hashimoto's thyroiditis → typically firm, irregular, non-bruitous goitre

  • Subacute (De Quervain) thyroiditis → painful/tender thyroid

  • De Quervain's thyroiditis = subacute granulomatous thyroiditis

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Graves → diffuse goitre + bruit

  • Graves → TSH receptor antibody (TRAb)

  • Hashimoto → anti-TPO, firm thyroid

  • De Quervain → painful thyroid + low radioactive iodine uptake

Exam Pearl:
Diffuse soft goitre + bruit = Graves' disease.

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ২২) Endocrine cause of headache excludes.....?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
Headache can occur with several endocrine disorders, particularly conditions involving pituitary enlargement or catecholamine excess.

  • Acromegaly → headache is common, partly due to pituitary enlargement.

  • Pituitary tumor → headache due to mass effect/raised pressure.

  • Pheochromocytoma → episodic severe headache is a classic symptom along with sweating and palpitations.

  • Thyrotoxicosis → headache can occur, but it is not a classic endocrine cause of headache compared with the other options.

Therefore, the best answer is thyrotoxicosis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Pheochromocytoma → headache + sweating + palpitations

  • Pituitary tumor → headache + visual field defects

  • Acromegaly → headache + enlarged hands/feet

  • Thyrotoxicosis → heat intolerance, weight loss, tremor, palpitations

Exam Pearl:
Endocrine causes of headache → think pituitary tumors, acromegaly, and pheochromocytoma.

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ২৩) Which is not a feature of thyrotoxicosis?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
Thyrotoxicosis typically causes oligomenorrhea or amenorrhea, rather than menorrhagia, due to disruption of the hypothalamic–pituitary–gonadal axis.

  • Weight loss → common feature

  • Heat intolerance → common feature

  • Palpitation → common due to increased sympathetic activity

  • Menorrhagia → not typical; thyrotoxicosis more commonly causes scanty/infrequent menstruation

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Thyrotoxicosis → weight loss + heat intolerance + tremor + palpitation

  • Menstrual disturbance → usually oligomenorrhea/amenorrhea

  • Hypothyroidism → classically menorrhagia

Exam Pearl:
Thyrotoxicosis → oligomenorrhea; hypothyroidism → menorrhagia.

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ২৪) Which is a feature of autonomic neuropathy?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
Postural (orthostatic) hypotension is a classic feature of autonomic neuropathy, especially in diabetic autonomic neuropathy. It occurs due to impaired sympathetic vasoconstriction when standing, causing an excessive fall in blood pressure.

  • Postural hypotension → autonomic dysfunction

  • Pain → commonly associated with sensory neuropathy

  • Sensory loss → peripheral sensory neuropathy

  • Motor weakness → motor neuropathy

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Autonomic neuropathy → postural hypotension, resting tachycardia, gastroparesis, bladder dysfunction, erectile dysfunction, sweating abnormalities.

  • Sensory neuropathy → numbness, tingling, pain, loss of sensation.

  • Motor neuropathy → weakness and muscle wasting.

Exam Pearl:
Autonomic neuropathy → postural hypotension.

Nervous, endocrine & skin.question: ২৫) Which is an intermediate acting insulin?
Nervous, endocrine & skin.exp:
Isophane insulin (NPH) is an intermediate-acting insulin, with an onset of approximately 1–2 hours and a duration of about 12–18 hours.

  • Lispro → rapid-acting

  • Aspart → rapid-acting

  • Isophane/NPH → intermediate-acting

  • Glargine → long-acting

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Insulin Type
Lispro Rapid-acting
Aspart Rapid-acting
Isophane (NPH) Intermediate-acting
Glargine Long-acting

Exam Pearl:
Intermediate-acting insulin = Isophane (NPH).
